To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“NF-κ B is a master regulator of miRNA expression and miRNA-mediated gene regulation in the human brain and NF-κ B is up-regulated and activated in the brains of patients with Alzheimer's disease” (Lukiw, 1997; Lukiw W.

NF-κ B-regulated miRNAtargets, and the resulting dysregulation of mRNA expression, play a major role in the pathogenesis of sporadic AD and that selective inhibition of the actions NF-κ B or specific miRNA species may be useful therapeutic approaches in AD.

NF-κ B up-regulated miRNA species are down-regulating the expression of key brain-specific mRNAs, including those encoding the amyloid precursor protein (APP), and that this may be contributing to the pathogenesis of AD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery of new NF-κ B-targeted anti-inflammatory drugs (NAT-ADs), and the development of novel anti-NF-κ B miRNA strategies to treat AD and related neurodegenerative disorders.

the identification and functional characterization of NF-κ- B-sensitive miRNas and their targets, and with the design of novel therapeutic strategies for the inhibition of their combined effects in the AD process.
the development of anti-inflammatory and anti-neurodegenerative therapeutics based on the inhibition of NF-κ-B-mediated miRNA expression in AD and other neurodegenerative diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NF-κ B pathway is the major culprit in the initiation and propagation, and the NF-κ - B-miRNA network the main driver, of the pathological gene expression programs in AD.
the NF-κ B pathway is a key regulator of the expression of many miRNAs, and that NF-κ B is a major contributor to the pathogenesis of AD.
NF-κB and NF-κB-sensitive miRNA up-regulation is pathogenic in AD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the NF-κB-sensitive miRNAs, miR-155 and miR-146a, are induced by NF-κB and that these miRNAs are down-regulated by NF-κ B antagonists, including NF-κB-IκBα super-repressors, and that the down-regulation or silencing of miR-155 or miR-146 a is neuroprotective in AD (Lukiw and Alexandrova, 2012).
the NF-κB-miRNA signaling network is a major contributor to the AD pathogenesis and that the NF- κ B-miRNA axis is a viable target for the development of new AD therapeutics.

the NF-κ B- and miRNA-mediated signaling networks in AD brain appear to be “out of control,” and this is due, in part to the chronic activation of NF-κ-B signaling pathways and the up-regulation of specific NF-κ-B-sensitive miRNAs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the up-regulation of specific miRNAs by NF-κ B in AD may be a key pathogenic event in the development of the neurodegenerative pathology in AD.

NF-κ B is a master regulator of miRNA gene transcription in human brain and other tissues, and that NF-κB-sensitive miRNAs are involved in the regulation of brain homeostatic and disease-related gene expression.
the up-regulation of miR-146a, miR-155 and miR-132 in AD is not beneficial to neuronal health and function.
